headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines with momentum fading; whales moving coins to cold storage while leverage crowds build, especially in alts.
paragraphs: The regime is intact but thinning. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, but only Ethereum and Solana show golden crosses, suggesting uptrend confirmation is spotty across the board. Dogecoin and Cardano have already broken below the 200-day line, putting them in a different structural posture than the majors. The month-to-date picture tells the story: Bitcoin up 16.2% on the month, Ethereum up 23.9%, Solana up 27.6%. Yet on the week, Bitcoin is down 0.5%, Ethereum down 2.9%, and Solana only up 4.4% despite its 200-day strength. The last few days have turned choppy. Bitcoin down 0.1% on the day, Ethereum down 1.1%, XRP down 0.1%. That reversal from month-long gains to recent weakness is a fracture worth noting, even if the longer structure has not broken.

Momentum indicators show neither acceleration nor alarm, but they are not aligned. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 65.1 with MACD below its signal line, a divergence: price strength without confirmatory oscillator energy. Ethereum's RSI is 61.3, also with MACD below signal, same story. Solana is the outlier: RSI 62.5 with MACD above signal, the one major showing both indicators in agreement. XRP, BNB, and the smaller names show RSI in the upper half but MACD negative or uncertain, a pattern of resting momentum rather than building conviction. These are not oversold conditions and not deeply overbought, but the lack of agreement between price position and momentum is a yellow flag. A market that moves without its momentum indicators confirming typically does not hold the move.

Positioning on the leverage side reveals crowding, especially in the alts. Bitcoin funding on OKX sits at 0.005% per 8 hours (5.5% annualized), moderate and stable. Ethereum is higher at 0.0072% per 8 hours (7.9% annualized), longs paying to hold. But XRP is at 0.01% per 8 hours (11% annualized) and Dogecoin also at 0.01% per 8 hours (11% annualized), the kind of sustained positive funding that signals longs are overextended. Solana, by contrast, is negative at minus 0.0013% per 8 hours (minus 1.4% annualized), shorts paying longs, a sign of exhaustion or positioning balance. Open interest across Bitcoin and Ethereum remains substantial (2.24 trillion and 1.57 trillion USD respectively), but the long-to-short ratios are the story: Ethereum 1.64 to 1, XRP 2.6 to 1, Dogecoin 4.13 to 1. That last ratio is dangerous. A four-to-one long bias with 11% annualized funding is a market built on borrowed conviction. Liquidations in the last six to eleven hours show shorts taking pain in Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Solana, but the damage is asymmetric: 712k in Bitcoin shorts liquidated versus 166k in longs; 1.2 million in Ethereum longs liquidated versus 230k in shorts. That is real tension between sides.

Whale behavior over the past 48 hours paints a different picture than the leverage crowd. Bitcoin moved 421 million USD off exchanges net, with 705 million leaving exchanges and only 284 million arriving. The biggest individual moves were 173 million off Coinbase and 156 million off Kraken, large wallets moving coins to cold storage. Over the same window, 321 million in USDC moved onto Coinbase in two transactions, classic pattern of dry powder being staged. The weekly view confirms the shift: weeks ending August 12, 19, and 26 saw money flowing onto exchanges (1.05 billion, 82 million, 1.58 billion respectively), but the week ending September 2 shows 344 million moving off exchanges. That is a regime change in just one week. Stablecoins sit at 309 billion USD total, up 1.17% over 30 days, modest fuel but present. ETF flows add nuance: Bitcoin ETF saw 7.3 million inflow on September 2 and 27.9 million net inflow over the last five sessions, but only one day in the same direction, so today's print is not a continuation of the five-day trend. Ethereum ETF is more consistent: 8.6 million inflow on September 1 and 616.5 million net inflow over five sessions with ten consecutive days in the same direction, a real bid from traditional finance.

The crowd sentiment sits at 63 on the Fear and Greed index, in the Greed zone but well below the 30-day high of 74. Over the last 30 days the gauge has ranged 25 to 74, a wide and volatile swing. Today's 63 is middle-of-the-road greed, not euphoria. The tape, however, does not match the sentiment precisely. Whales are rotating into cold storage (supply reduction) while leverage longs build funding costs (demand through borrowed capital). Traditional finance is buying (ETF inflows), but crypto natives are moving coins away. That is a disconnect worth watching. The market has held above 200-day lines, but momentum is not confirming, and the concentration of long positioning in the altcoin complex with high funding rates is fragile. Bitcoin dominance sits at 59.1%, a moderate share, and total market cap down 2.58% on the day.

Watch for three conditions: a break below the 200-day line for Bitcoin or Ethereum (structural regime shift), a funding flip in XRP or Doge from positive to negative (shorts gaining relief and longs capitulating), and a reversal in the whale off-exchange flow back onto exchanges in the next 48 hours (signal that storage accumulation is complete or conviction is fading). The daily price action is weak, but the monthly trend is still positive and the big money is moving coins off venue. That combination usually persists for a window, but only if momentum refreshes or positioning relieves pressure. The read today is patience with caution.
